# npistat

[![R-CMD-check](https://github.com/mtloots/npistat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/mtloots/npistat/actions/workflows/R-CMD-check.yaml)

**Nonparametric predictive inference** for censored and Bernoulli data: lower and upper
probabilities for future observations under Hill's assumption A(n), carried by M-functions.

* For data censored on the right, the left or within intervals of arbitrary width: the M-functions of
  a sharing assumption that reproduces the right-censored theory of Coolen and Yan (2004) exactly,
  and survival bounds for the next observation that contain the Turnbull estimator under every
  censoring pattern.
* For Bernoulli data: bounds on the number of events among several future observations
  (Coolen 1998), and the same bounds from censored data by completions.

Computation runs on a shared pure-C back-end that is also bound from Python, and the two front
ends are checked against each other value by value.

## Installation

```r
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mtloots/npistat", subdir = "npistat")
```

## Usage

The six-observation right-censored example of Yan (2002), in units of 1/35:

```{r example}
library(npistat)
tm <- c(3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9); ev <- c(1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1)
s <- npi_survival(tm, ifelse(ev == 1, tm, Inf), t = c(5, 7.5, 9.5))
transform(s, lower35 = lower * 35, upper35 = upper * 35)
```

Interval-censored data, with the members of the construction and the Turnbull set:

```{r interval}
L <- c(3.5, 3.4, 4.7, 6.9, 5.6, 2.4); R <- c(6.5, 6.8, 5.9, 6.9, 7.9, 6.4)
npi_survival(L, R, t = 5.75, members = TRUE)
```

A portfolio of 1000 obligors with two defaults: bounds on the number of defaults among the next 100.

```{r bernoulli}
npi_bernoulli(n = 1000, k = 2, m = 100, r = 1:5)
```
